## Rule

ARC-GEN source-read: `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_6d0160f0.py`.

The 11×11 active grid is a 3×3 board of 3×3 mini-grids separated by gray rows/cols at 3 and 7. Exactly one yellow pixel appears inside one source mini-grid. Its mini-grid coordinate `(br, bc)` selects the source block; its local coordinate `(lr, lc)` selects the destination block. Output is a fresh 11×11 board with gray separators, the selected source 3×3 mini-grid copied into destination block `(lr, lc)`, and all other mini-cells black. Outside 11×11 is all-zero padding.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
out = hollywood_squares(3, black=0, separator=5)
yr, yc = location_of_color(input, 4)
br, bc = yr // 4, yc // 4
dr, dc = yr % 4, yc % 4
for rr in range(3):
    for cc in range(3):
        out[4 * dr + rr][4 * dc + cc] = input[4 * br + rr][4 * bc + cc]
```

ONNX v8 avoids the charged canvas entirely. It uses one final direct `Einsum` over the original one-hot input twice: one copy supplies source pixels, the other supplies the unique yellow marker gate. Factored block/local maps route source block `(br, bc)` and marker local coordinate `(lr, lc)` to the output block, while rank-11 channel bases emit copied nonblack channels, default black mini-cells, and gray separators. The full 10×30×30 threshold tensor is the final output, so no full-size intermediate is charged.

## Cost analysis

> **NOTE (batch56 2026-07-09):** the v10=744 analysis below is SUPERSEDED. LIVE is Aditya's
> **392** single-Einsum free-output (`signrank3`). Floor proof for 392 is in
> `hard_records/free_output_pad_tail_sweep.md`. `floor_est 156` is STALE (it assumed a charged
> `[1,10,H,W]` prepad — already deleted; the live graph has memory=0). **392 is at the floor.**
>
> Forced components (each proven — ablation / orthogonality / structure):
> - Channel C,S=80 rank-4 minimal: `ch0−ch5` const is orthogonal (lstsq err √2) to the rank-3
>   circular copy code ⇒ a 4th channel component is required.
> - Spatial D4,M4=240 rank-4 minimal: dest-placement contracts `BL[x,D]` with D∈{0,1,2} ⇒ block
>   rank ≥3 (rank-2 simplex structurally can't index placement); separators are placed by the
>   product `D4·M4` ⇒ sep must be nonzero in BOTH factors (`D4[:,3]==M4[:,3]==SEP`, both
>   load-bearing) — the "duplication" is forced, not wasteful.
> - Glue B,T,P=50 + Y=10: every row ablation-load-bearing.
>
> Free-identity rank-3 copy (BL[30,3]+LO[30,3]+SEP[30]=210) is VERIFIED 267/267 in numpy but
> can't fold to one free-output Einsum < 392: the channel-flow identity dies on folding (needs
> rank-4 C/S back), and a 2nd node makes the copy a charged `[1,10,30,30]` intermediate (~18 KB).

### (superseded) Staged v10: `cost=744 = memory 0 + params 744`, `profile_cost=744`.

Charged params:
- `D`, `M`: 30×3 block/local row factors, reused for source row/col, marker row/col, and output row/col = 180 params.
- CP output-map factors `TD`, `XD`, `UD`, `TM`, `XM`, `LM`: copied cells, mini-cell constants, and active 11×11 gray rectangle = 324 params.
- `A`, `C`, `S`: rank-10 channel bases = 230 params. Source mini-cells cannot be gray in ARC-GEN (`random_colors(..., exclude=[gray, yellow])`, then one cell is changed to yellow), so v10 drops the source-color-5 copy rank while keeping gray separator output in the constant term.
- `Y`: second-input yellow-channel selector = 10 params.

Architecture floor verdict: direct final-output contraction is the winning route here. The single-channel-canvas family bottoms out around the 900 B full canvas plus sampler/assembly tensors; v8 removed the canvas and all intermediate tensors, v9 compressed the output masks, and v10 removes an impossible color rank from the copied-source channel basis. Further safe reductions likely require a new way to express the 30×3 block/local maps or the explicit 10-entry yellow-channel selector.

## Don't-do log

- Do not trust the `Pattern_Recognition / Symmetry Completion` label as the rule. The generator rule is yellow-local-coordinate block copy.
- Do not use plain `MatMul(UINT8)`: ONNX shape inference rejects it (`A typestr: T, has unsupported type: tensor(uint8)`). Use unit-scale `QLinearMatMul` for the 9×9 u8 contraction.
- Do not decode the whole 11×11 color-index plane then gather non-separator cells unless simplicity is worth the extra cost. The strided local-cell sampler is 728 B cheaper than the full 11×11/gather v4 route.
- Do not put full-input operands first in the direct final `Einsum`. The same 1,390-param equation was correct but took ~7.5s for 10 official pairs; gate-first operand order took ~0.02s for the same sample.
- Do not stage direct-Einsum variants on visible alone. v10 has full ARC-GEN truth and full A-B; keep that bar because the final contraction is easy to perturb with a label typo.
- Do not re-add a source-gray copy rank unless the generator changes. Source mini-grid colors exclude gray; separator gray is a separate constant-output term.
- (batch56) Do not chase `floor_est 156` / the "delete charged prepad" direction — STALE. The LIVE 392 graph is already a clean single-Einsum free-output (memory=0). Nothing to dissolve.
- (batch56) Do not try to dedup the SEP column (D4[:,3]==M4[:,3]): forced by the 2-factor `D4·M4` separator placement — removing it needs a ones[30] back (net 0).
- (batch56) Do not try a rank-3 channel: `ch0−ch5` is orthogonal (lstsq err √2) to the rank-3 circular copy code — the 4th channel row is mathematically required.
- (batch56) Do not try rank-2 simplex spatial: dest-placement `BL[x,D]` needs one-hot rank-3 indexing; simplex is structurally incompatible (and leaks −0.5). 392 is the forced floor.
